clue.text: Set off without a meal

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the meal goes round the article

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: Someone sets out on a journey without stopping to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: LUNCH is placed around A.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch something is to start it going, as a ship or a campaign is set off.

clue.text: Article to provoke Army Command

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to tease is to provoke or taunt

explanation.surface: An item designed to provoke the army's high command.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand at ease is a military order relaxing the ranks.

clue.text: Brass thread patterned in decorative collar

parts.note: brass and neck both mean cheek or impudence
lace is thread worked into a pattern

explanation.surface: Brass wire and patterned thread are used in an ornamental collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like the metal but means nerve or cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is an ornament worn round the neck, like a jewelled collar.

clue.text: Crime in dwelling one police force discovered

indicators.note: in places the one and the police force inside the dwelling

parts.note: a home is a dwelling
I is the Roman numeral one
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A crime is found inside a house by a detective force.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the detective branch of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Homicide is the killing of a person, a serious crime.

clue.text: One' who sides with skilled worker on very little money

indicators.note: on in an across clue sets the skilled worker after the money, written to its right

parts.note: P, a penny, is the smallest coin of British money
an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: Someone takes the side of a poorly paid craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray mark after 'One' is a speck on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a committed supporter of a party or cause, someone who takes sides.

clue.text: Cross-country carriage left on time

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A coach leaves on schedule for a trip across country.
explanation.definitionFit: Portage is carrying boats or goods overland between waterways.

clue.text: Easter people — in temporary accommodation getting permanent home

indicators.note: in places the easterner and the people inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
read as East-er; E is the standard abbreviation for East
men means people

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers at Easter camp in tents, then get a permanent house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easter' is not the festival but one from the east, giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building divided into flats where people live, a lasting dwelling.

clue.text: Want to follow closely in support

indicators.note: in places the following word inside the prop

parts.note: a shore is a prop or support
to tag is to follow someone closely

explanation.surface: A wish to tail someone while also backing them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as a verb but is the noun, a lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or deficiency, an insufficient supply.

clue.text: Plain diamonds in uncommon clasp

indicators.note: clasp means the uncommon word holds the diamonds within its grip

parts.note: notable means remarkable, out of the common run
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Simple diamonds set in an unusual clasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like the adjective for simple, but it means obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain as in clear or evident, easily seen.

clue.text: Designer of engine almost runs into one just arriving

indicators.note: almost means the engineer's name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Thomas Newcomen designed the early atmospheric steam engine of 1712
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An engine designer nearly crashes into someone who has only just turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer is a recent arrival, someone new to a place.

clue.text: Peacemakers encountering quarrel open the door?

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeepers
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers meet a dispute and ask whether to let it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' reads as an argument but is the short arrow fired from a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbolt a door is to draw back its bolt so it can be opened; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Spicy act I developed outside Italian city

indicators.note: outside means the reworked letters wrap round the city
developed suggests the letters of act I being worked into a new form

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome

explanation.surface: A theatre's first act is made spicier around an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' turns ACT I into ATIC, which goes 'outside' ROMA: A-ROMA-TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means fragrant or pungent, as spices are.

clue.text: Ominous return of corporal punishment in China

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the Chinese dynasty

parts.note: Ming was a Chinese dynasty, famed for its porcelain

indicators.note: return of means the punishment word is read backwards

parts.note: the cane was a school corporal punishment

explanation.surface: Corporal punishment is being brought back in China, which looks threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns CANE into ENAC, which goes 'in' MING.
explanation.definitionFit: Menacing means threatening, so it is a synonym of ominous.

clue.text: Deceptive motorway double bend. ahead

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI
the letter S has the shape of a double bend
leading means in front, ahead

explanation.surface: A misleading sign on a motorway warns of a double bend.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; the 1 is written as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Misleading means giving a false impression, as deceptive does.

clue.text: It is scattered about on the way to get married

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
re means about or concerning
to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: Something is thrown about along the route to a wedding, like confetti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is scattered' sounds like confetti thrown on the way to church, but only 'scattered' defines; 'on' sets the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewed is a past form of strew, to spread or scatter things about.

clue.text: Keep back son required to put in further exercise

indicators.note: to put in means the son is placed within the training word

parts.note: to retrain is to train again

explanation.surface: A coach holds back a son who needs extra training.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep in check.

clue.text: Turn to instrument for passage of .. moving air

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as a handle
a pipe is a wind instrument

explanation.surface: Someone turns to a pipe, which needs air moved through it.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots in the clue are specks on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe or trachea is the tube carrying breath to the lungs.

clue.text: Someone different in lead .-Basil, for example

indicators.note: in puts the different person inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
another person is the other one

explanation.surface: A different person takes the lead role, perhaps a man called Basil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' looks like a man's name but is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a herb grown for the kitchen pot, a culinary herb.

clue.text: Old. Master's 'restoration incorporating new working

indicators.note: restoration suggests the letters of master are reworked, as an old picture is restored

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: Restoring an Old Master painting involves a new technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restoration incorporating new' rearranges MASTER with N.
explanation.definitionFit: On stream means in operation or production, working.

clue.text: It comes near the end of term to provide great amusement

indicators.note: comes near the end of means the word It is placed close to the term's last letter

parts.note: Hilary term is the spring term at Oxford and in the English law courts

explanation.surface: Something arriving towards the close of a school term brings much fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is the name of the term running from January to Easter at Oxford and in English courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity means boisterous merriment or laughter.

clue.text: Having edge, about to declare to set up win.

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the assembled word is read upwards
about means the edge word goes round the declaring word

parts.note: a lip is an edge or rim
to aver is to declare

explanation.surface: A team with the edge is about to claim victory.
explanation.walkthrough: LIP goes 'about' AVER to make LIAVERP, which 'set up' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to triumph or win through.

clue.text: Determined to reverse English failure about workers

indicators.note: to reverse means the whole assembled piece is read backwards
about means the English failure goes round the workers

parts.note: a loser is a failure
TU, a trade union, is a body of workers

explanation.surface: Someone is resolved to turn around an English flop with the help of the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' acts on the whole assembly, not just English: the run ETULOSER is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute means firm of purpose, fixed on a course.

clue.text: Notes from bird circling height, showing excitement

indicators.note: circling means the bird's notes go round the height

parts.note: a trill is a warbling run of birdsong notes

explanation.surface: Birdsong from on high gives a listener a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a sudden sensation of excitement or pleasure.

clue.text: Doctor's prescription, perhaps date on it is wrong

indicators.note: is wrong suggests the letters of date on it are in the wrong order and must be fixed

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription carries a mistaken date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' rearranges DATE ON IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote counters a poison, and is one thing a doctor might prescribe.

clue.text: It's used to dye one type of cloth

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
satin is a glossy fabric

explanation.surface: Something used to colour a particular fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatin is a red crystalline compound used in making dyes such as indigo.

clue.text: Single ingredient in a fresh casing provided as appetite whetter

indicators.note: ingredient in says the single letter is a part placed within the next words
casing confirms those words form a shell round the single letter

parts.note: fresh means cheeky, pert
I is the Roman numeral one, single
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A single item wrapped in a fresh case is served to whet the appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'ingredient in' and 'casing' signal the same container; 'fresh' means cheeky here, not new.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is a drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Basic material for Browning, for example

definitions.text: Basic material for Browning, for example

parts.words: Basic material for Browning, for example
parts.note: Browning reads as the poet or a browning process, but it is a make of firearm, and this alloy is what such weapons were made of

explanation.surface: Raw material for the poet Browning's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning is the gun maker, not the poet: an alloy of copper and tin once used for cannon.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronze alloy traditionally used for casting guns, so the stuff a firearm is made from.

clue.text: Insect not certain to get airborne?

parts.note: may expresses possibility, something not certain
to fly is to get into the air

explanation.surface: An insect unsure whether it can take off.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayfly is a short-lived winged insect.
